ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The lower wire in the circuit is the reference ground. On the left there is a 4∠0° A current source, with the arrow upward, injecting current into node V1. Between node V1 and ground, an impedance -j3 Ω is connected. Between node V2 and ground there are two branches: a 6 Ω resistor and a j6 Ω impedance. Between V1 and V2 there is a 4 Ω resistor, and at the same time a 10∠0° V voltage source is connected in parallel above it, with the left terminal of the voltage source positive and the right terminal negative, so its constraint is V1 - V2 = 10. Reasoning: Since the 10∠0° V voltage source is directly connected between V1 and V2, regard V1 and V2 as a supernode. The polarity of this voltage source gives V1 - V2 = 10, so V1 = V2 + 10. Write KCL for the supernode containing V1 and V2, taking the current leaving the supernode and flowing to ground as positive. The 4 A current source injects current into the supernode, so it is written as -4: V1/(-j3) + V2/6 + V2/(j6) - 4 = 0. Substituting V1 = V2 + 10 gives (j/3)(V2 + 10) + (1/6 - j/6)V2 = 4. Combining the V2 terms: [(j/3) + (1/6 - j/6)]V2 + 10j/3 = 4, that is (1/6 + j/6)V2 = 4 - 10j/3. Therefore V2 = (4 - 10j/3)/(1/6 + j/6) = 2 - j22 V.

method.method_draft: First identify V1 and V2 as a supernode because the 10∠0° V source is directly between them, with polarity giving V1 - V2 = 10. Write KCL for the combined supernode to ground: V1/(-j3) + V2/6 + V2/(j6) - 4 = 0, where the 4 A current source injects current into the supernode, hence appears as -4 for currents leaving. Substitute V1 = V2 + 10 and solve the single complex equation: (j/3)(V2+10) + (1/6 - j/6)V2 = 4. Rearranging gives (1/6 + j/6)V2 = 4 - 10j/3, so V2 = (4 - 10j/3)/(1/6 + j/6) = 2 - j22 V.
